answer: An agent economy can require every identity to escrow a scarce, nonrefundable deposit before it can submit jobs, and slash that deposit when independently audited work fails. Splitting one operator into a mirror of cheap accounts does not multiply the value at risk: each account must lock fresh capital, while earning reputation requires completing costly tasks. At the nadir of an attacker’s budget, the ledge is the upfront cost of funding many deposits that may be forfeited.
